title: MEXT Student Guidance Survey: Institutional Vigilance, Bullying Recognition, and Alternative Digital Attendance in Japan
source_name: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT)
description: Annual nationwide census monitoring student guidance dynamics across Japanese primary and lower secondary schools, exploring the relationship between proactive bullying reporting, counselor interventions, chronic absenteeism, and digital learning attendance recognition.
observation_unit: School stage longitudinal panel across primary and lower secondary institutions in Japan
sample_population_note: Annual census of all public and private elementary and junior high schools in Japan (approx. 29,000 institutions)
title_ja: 【児童生徒の問題行動・不登校調査】いじめ積極認知と不登校代替出席認定の多変量分析

research_angles.title: The Institutional Vigilance Paradox: How Aggressive Bullying Recognition and Alternative Digital Attendance Reshape Student Safety Nets
research_questions: Does higher reported bullying incidence indicate deteriorating school safety, or institutional vigilance that facilitates support?
Has the expansion of ICT-recognized alternative attendance provided a viable safety net for non-attending students?
hypotheses: Reported bullying incidents and counselor intervention hours exhibit strong positive covariance without multicollinearity (VIF < 2.0), reflecting proactive institutional detection.
ICT recognized alternative attendance has expanded rapidly, moderating the severity of academic disengagement for chronic absentees.
research_angles.theoretical_framework: Ecological Systems Theory (Bronfenbrenner) and Institutional Safety Net Framework
